title: Tauri: grant per-file runtime fs scope when opening .fla outside scoped dirs
description:
Task 1394 narrowed the desktop static fs scope to content dirs; opening a .fla outside them then failed. FIX (per-file RUNTIME scope, static capability unchanged):
- src-tauri/src/lib.rs: new #[tauri::command] allow_fs_path(app, path) -> app.fs_scope().allow_file(path) (tauri-plugin-fs 2.5.1 FsExt runtime Scope). Registered via invoke_handler(generate_handler![allow_fs_path]). Per-file only (NOT per-directory) so opening a file in ~ does not re-expose home; grant lasts the app session. App-local command needs no ACL entry.
- authoring-ui/src/hooks/tauriFsScope.ts: grantRuntimeFsScope(path) invokes allow_fs_path; no-op outside Tauri / empty path; best-effort (errors logged, not thrown, so the subsequent read/write surfaces the real message).
- Wired into every dialog site before readFile/writeFile: useFileActions openDocument, saveDocument(known path), saveDocumentAs, exportBinaryFla, importToLibrary, importSoundToLibrary, probeVideoFile; usePublish publishToFile.
- authoring-ui package.json: added @tauri-apps/api (^2.0.0) direct dep for @tauri-apps/api/core invoke (was only transitive; pnpm strict).
- docs/00-overview-and-architecture.md: Desktop shell security section updated (per-file runtime scope subsection + manual-verify step for an out-of-scope .fla).
TESTS (packages/authoring-ui, vitest): src/__tests__/tauriFsScope.test.ts (4: no-op non-Tauri / empty path; invokes allow_fs_path with chosen path; swallows errors) + src/__tests__/fileActionsScope.test.ts (2: openDocument grants scope BEFORE readFile; publishToFile grants BEFORE writeFile, for an out-of-scope path). 6/6 pass.
VERIFY: full ordered build 'pnpm --filter ./packages/** build' exit 0; '@flash/desktop typecheck' exit 0; 3 tauri JSONs well-formed. Tauri binary build/run is manual (headless) - Rust command validated against vendored tauri-plugin-fs 2.5.1 / tauri 2.11.2 Scope API (allow_file signature confirmed). Pre-existing unrelated failure: collab presenceRender.test.ts (2, fails on clean origin/main too).
